answer: One concrete mechanism is stake-weighted task bonding: each agent must lock tokens behind a verifiable identity before receiving work, and rewards unlock only after peers attest completed tasks. A sock-puppet attacker must fund hundreds of separate stakes plus fees, so flooding the network turns into a costly race against the tide of honest capital. Reputation then flows like a river, carrying trust only to agents whose history survives scrutiny, while a lone falcon swooping in with fresh wallets gains nothing without sustained stake and peer attestations.
